A child inheriting a rental house does not automatically inherit its low assessed value. Indexed limits should be checked with BOE rather than memorized as permanently fixed.

672.title: Transfer tax and prorations
672.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
672.text: Use the stated tax base and day-count convention, then assign debits and credits according to who already paid or collected the item. The common county documentary transfer tax authorized by Revenue and Taxation Code section 11911 is $0.55 per $500, or fraction, of the applicable taxable value. Value of qualifying liens remaining on the property is excluded under that provision. City taxes and local rules can add costs. A new purchase loan is not automatically a remaining old lien for this calculation. If the stated taxable amount is $620,000 and only that county rate applies, divide by $500 to obtain 1,240 units, then multiply by $0.55: $682. Round units upward when a fractional $500 unit exists, not to the nearest whole unit. For prorations, identify who already paid or collected the item and who should bear it for each period. Suppose annual taxes are $7,200 and the problem specifies a 360-day year. The daily amount is $20. If the seller owes 40 days that remain unpaid and the buyer will pay them, debit the seller and credit the buyer $800. If the seller already prepaid the buyer's 40-day share, reverse those entries. Use actual-day or 30-day conventions only when the problem or instructions specify them.

673.title: Rent and taxes run in opposite directions
673.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
673.text: A seller receives the full $3,000 rent for a thirty-day month before a sale. The contract assigns the first ten days to the seller and the remaining twenty days to the buyer. The seller collected $2,000 belonging economically to the buyer's period, so debit the seller and credit the buyer $2,000. That entry reallocates income already received. Now assume the seller prepaid $600 of a charge covering the same month and the contract uses the same allocation. The buyer owes twenty-thirtieths, or $400, so debit the buyer and credit the seller $400. The direction reverses because the seller advanced an expense for the buyer's period. Netting the two prorations produces a $1,600 credit to the buyer, but calculate each separately before combining them. Do not invent who owns the closing day. A question may assign that day to either party or specify an exact count. Nor should an annual charge automatically use a 360-day year unless the stated convention permits it. First identify the amount, covered period, allocation, and payment status. The debit and credit then follow from who owes whom.

674.title: Exam review
674.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
674.text: Label each calculation before using a percentage or subtraction; correct arithmetic on debt, basis, proceeds, or taxable gain cannot repair a mistaken category. Cash proceeds are not taxable gain; withholding is a prepayment, not final liability.Income-tax basis, property-tax assessed value, and market value are different quantities.Proposition 13 separates the 1% general levy from the maximum 2% annual inflation increase in factored base-year value.Reassessment events and Proposition 8 recovery can produce assessed-value increases greater than 2%.Exclusion is not deferral, and a property-tax exclusion is not an income-tax exclusion.Write the calculation base, payment status, and stated day-count convention before calculating prorations.

675.title: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations: core distinctions
675.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
675.text: Three gains Realized, recognized, and deferred gain are different quantities. Cash Debt payoff and withholding affect cash without necessarily reducing realized gain. Two assessment tracks Proposition 8 temporarily reduces assessed value without replacing the Proposition 13 factored ceiling.

676.title: Cash boot without losing the entire deferral
676.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
676.text: Assume a fully qualifying investment-property exchange. Relinquished property has a $700,000 fair market value and $400,000 adjusted basis. The taxpayer receives replacement real property worth $650,000 plus $50,000 cash. There is no debt, exchange expense, depreciation-recapture complication, related-party issue, or other adjustment. The exercise isolates ordinary cash boot; eligibility and timing are stipulated, not inferred from these numbers. Recognized gain is a current tax category, deferred gain is preserved for later treatment, and basis carries that preservation forward. These figures do not prove exchange eligibility; actual transactions require timely identification, receipt, and compliance with the other governing requirements.

677.title: Any boot makes the whole exchange taxable.
677.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
677.text: Compare realized gain with the relevant boot under the applicable rules. Cash can cause partial recognition rather than destroy every deferral.

678.title: Deferred means permanently excluded.
678.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
678.text: Track the replacement property's basis. A lower basis preserves gain for later tax treatment.

679.title: Every annual assessed-value increase is limited to 2%.
679.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
679.text: Check reassessment events and whether a temporary Proposition 8 reduction is recovering. The factored base-year ceiling continues separately; recovery toward it can exceed 2% of the prior reduced assessment.

680.title: Cash boot without losing the entire deferral: Find realized gain
680.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
680.text: Relinquished property value $700,000 Adjusted basis $400,000 Replacement property value $650,000 Cash received $50,000 700000 - 400000 300000 The exchange produces $300,000 of economic gain before applying the nonrecognition rule. Receiving real property rather than only cash does not prevent gain from being realized. The $650,000 replacement value plus $50,000 cash accounts for the $700,000 received in this simplified exchange.

681.title: Cash boot without losing the entire deferral: Limit current recognition
681.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
681.text: Relinquished property value $700,000 Adjusted basis $400,000 Replacement property value $650,000 Cash received $50,000 min(300000, 50000) 50000 With only the stated cash boot and no complicating adjustments, recognize the lesser of realized gain and cash received. The taxpayer does not recognize the whole $300,000 merely because some cash was received. Conversely, boot cannot create recognized gain greater than the total gain actually realized.

682.title: Cash boot without losing the entire deferral: Identify deferred gain
682.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
682.text: Relinquished property value $700,000 Adjusted basis $400,000 Replacement property value $650,000 Cash received $50,000 300000 - 50000 250000 The remaining $250,000 is deferred, not permanently excluded. This number is not a tax payment, a lender payoff, or additional spendable cash. The final tax on the recognized portion depends on applicable tax rules and the taxpayer's circumstances, none of which are supplied by this calculation.

683.title: Cash boot without losing the entire deferral: Carry the deferral into basis
683.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
683.text: Relinquished property value $700,000 Adjusted basis $400,000 Replacement property value $650,000 Cash received $50,000 650000 - 250000 400000 Subtract deferred gain from the replacement property's fair market value to obtain its simplified $400,000 basis. A later taxable sale can therefore reveal the preserved gain. Assigning a fresh $650,000 basis while also deferring $250,000 would improperly erase the very gain the exchange rules postponed.

684.title: Cash boot without losing the entire deferral: Test an unchanged-value later sale
684.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
684.text: Relinquished property value $700,000 Adjusted basis $400,000 Replacement property value $650,000 Cash received $50,000 650000 - 400000 250000 If the replacement property were later sold in a fully taxable sale for the same $650,000 value, with no intervening basis changes or selling expenses, the gain would be $250,000. That matches the amount previously deferred. Do not subtract the earlier $50,000 recognized gain again; it was already accounted for in establishing replacement basis.

685.title: Sale proceeds are not the same as taxable gain
685.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
685.text: Sale proceeds are not the same as taxable gain With an assumed $500,000 adjusted basis, realized gain is $760,000 amount realized minus $500,000 basis = $260,000 before any exclusion or deferral. The loan payoff affects cash, not that gain calculation. Illustrative selling price 800000 Assumed selling expenses -40000 Loan payoff -300000 Illustrative cash proceeds 460000 Before other settlement debits, credits, or withholding.

686.title: Payment status determines the proration direction
686.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
686.text: Payment status determines the proration direction Use the stated day count and closing-day allocation. Income already collected and expenses already advanced can produce opposite entries for the same ownership period. Who has already paid or received the amount allocated to the other party? Seller prepaid buyer expense The seller advanced a charge allocated to the buyer's period. Debit buyer; credit seller. Buyer will pay seller expense The seller's allocated share is unpaid and will be paid by the buyer. Debit seller; credit buyer. Seller collected buyer rent The seller already received rent allocated to the buyer's period. Debit seller; credit buyer.

687.title: Market value and enrolled value need not match
687.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
687.text: Market value and enrolled value need not match An educational value comparison, not a county form. Assessed value and the eventual tax bill are different quantities. Annual assessment / Value summary Original fictional excerpt for ordinary real property. Assume no reassessable event, exemptions, disaster adjustment, or other special rule. A $750,000 market estimate does not automatically produce a $750,000 assessment for this continuing owner. Valuation date January 1 The annual lien-date comparison does not use the November installment due date. Current market value $750,000 This estimates current value. Appreciation alone does not reset the Proposition 13 baseline. Factored base-year value $430,000 This follows the existing base-year history and permitted annual inflation adjustments. Enrolled assessed value $430,000 The lesser applicable value is enrolled. None of these fields establishes the owner's income-tax basis. Read a fictional assessment summary without substituting market value for the applicable factored base-year value.

688.title: Cap the factor, then compound the value
688.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
688.text: Cap the factor, then compound the value Assume no reassessment, decline-in-value reduction, or other adjustment. This is assessed-value growth, not a property-tax rate calculation. Starting base-year value 500000 First increase: 1% of $500,000 5000 Next increase: capped 2% of $505,000 10100 Factored base-year value 515100 The second year uses $505,000, not the original $500,000. Hypothetical 4% inflation is capped at 2% for that adjustment. Apply a one-percent adjustment followed by a capped two-percent adjustment to the correct preceding factored value.

689.title: Temporary reductions do not reset the ceiling
689.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
689.text: Temporary reductions do not reset the ceiling Compare both values at each lien date. The reduced Year 1 assessment does not become a new Proposition 13 base year. Assume successive January 1 valuations, a 2% annual inflation factor, and no ownership change, construction, exemption change, or other adjustment. The 2% cap governs growth of the factored ceiling. Recovery from a temporarily reduced assessment can be greater than 2%. Temporary reduction Year 1 Factored ceiling $600,000; market $520,000. Enroll the lower $520,000. Market recovers below the ceiling Year 2 Ceiling $612,000; market $580,000. Enroll $580,000, an 11.54% increase from the prior reduced assessment. Restore the factored ceiling Year 3 Ceiling $624,240; market $650,000. Enroll $624,240 rather than the higher market value. Track Proposition 8 recovery while the independent factored base-year ceiling continues to grow.

690.title: Reassess the interest or construction that changed
690.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
690.text: Reassess the interest or construction that changed Independent simplified alternatives, not successive events. Routine maintenance generally is not new construction; statutory exclusions and special ownership rules require separate review. Assume a $400,000 existing factored value, no exclusion, and no other adjustment. Which independent event occurs? Reassessable transfer of the whole property Fair market value at transfer is $900,000. The whole transferred interest receives a $900,000 new base-year value. Ordinary reassessable transfer of a 50% interest The whole property is worth $900,000; the other half does not change ownership. Retain $200,000 for the unchanged half; add $450,000 for the transferred half: $650,000. Completed addition with no ownership change The addition contributes $100,000 of market value, regardless of whether its construction cost differs. Retain $400,000 for the unaffected property; add $100,000: $500,000. Distinguish whole-property reassessment from partial-interest reassessment and the increment added by new construction.

691.title: The general levy is one part of the bill
691.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
691.text: The general levy is one part of the bill The illustrative bill totals $7,220. All additions are assumed authorized; neither 1.12% nor the $500 charge is a statewide universal rate. General levy 1% of $600,000 taxable assessed value 6000 Permitted bond debt Stipulated 0.12% of the same $600,000 base 720 Direct assessment Stipulated lawful fixed charge, not another value percentage 500 Separate the one-percent ad valorem levy from authorized debt rates and a fixed direct assessment.

692.title: A supplemental bill taxes the change in value
692.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
692.text: A supplemental bill taxes the change in value Original educational extract, not a county bill. An October event ordinarily creates one supplemental bill for the affected fiscal year. Supplemental assessment / Calculation extract Fictional October 15 sale. Assume assessed value rises from $400,000 to $600,000, a 1.1% applicable ad valorem rate, and no exemptions or other adjustments. A later supplemental bill need not be covered by closing prorations or the lender's impound account. Check its own payment instructions. Supplemental assessed value $600,000 - $400,000 = $200,000 Tax the increase, not the whole $600,000 again. The existing annual bill remains separate. Annual tax on the increase $200,000 x 0.011 = $2,200 Apply the stated ad valorem rate before the statutory partial-year factor. Effective date and factor November 1 / 0.67 Start the month after the event. Section 75.41 specifies 0.67; do not replace it with exact 8/12. Supplemental tax $2,200 x 0.67 = $1,474 This statutory calculation is not the buyer-seller debit and credit used to allocate expenses at closing. Read the assessment increase and statutory monthly factor without taxing the full property value twice or substituting a contractual proration convention.

693.title: A depreciated gift has a no-gain, no-loss interval
693.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
693.text: A depreciated gift has a no-gain, no-loss interval Fictional investment land, no intervening adjustments or selling costs. Deductibility and tax character are separate from calculating the gain or loss. Amount realized on later sale Calculated gain or loss At $375,000, the gain calculation is negative and the loss calculation is positive. The dual-basis rule yields neither gain nor loss, not a choice of the more favorable basis. Gift: $400,000 donor basis; $350,000 gift-date value 300000 -50000 350000 0 375000 0 400000 0 450000 50000 Choose the donor basis for gain and gift-date fair market value for loss when the gift value is lower.

694.title: A joint return does not automatically double the exclusion
694.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
694.text: A joint return does not automatically double the exclusion Fictional eligibility contrasts. The exclusion offsets qualifying gain, not the sales price or loan payoff. Spouses file jointly. Assume no automatic disqualification, nonqualified-use allocation or depreciation issue. Who satisfies the tests? One owner; both residents One spouse owned for two of the prior five years. Both used the home for that period and meet the two-year look-back rule. The ordinary $500,000 maximum can apply; both spouses need not hold title for two years. One fails residence Only one spouse meets the residence test; no partial-exclusion exception is stipulated. The ordinary joint $500,000 test is not met. Evaluate each spouse's eligibility rather than automatically doubling. Recent prior exclusion One spouse used the exclusion on another sale less than two years earlier. The look-back condition for the ordinary joint maximum fails; investigate any applicable separate or partial relief. Apply the ownership, use and look-back conditions separately to spouses.

695.title: The exchange clocks start together
695.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
695.text: The exchange clocks start together Calendar-day arithmetic; January 16 is day zero. All other exchange conditions, including restrictions on receiving sale proceeds, still apply. Fictional deferred exchange: relinquished property transfers January 16, 2026. Assume the tax-return due date including extensions is later than the 180th day, with no special relief. The ordinary outside period is not 45 plus 180 days. An earlier tax-return due date, including extensions, can shorten the receipt period. Transfer starts both periods January 16 Do not wait for identification before starting the 180-day count. Identification boundary March 2 / Day 45 Make the required signed written identification and timely delivery to an eligible recipient. Receipt boundary July 15 / Day 180 Receive qualifying identified replacement property by this date under the stated return-date assumption. Calculate the identification and receipt periods from the relinquished-property transfer.

696.title: Cash received, gain recognized, and replacement basis
696.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
696.text: Cash received, gain recognized, and replacement basis Original hypothetical, not an exchange recommendation. Debt relief, exchange costs and other property require additional rules. Exchange worksheet / Cash-only boot Fictional investment land: old adjusted basis $280,000; replacement land worth $390,000 plus $30,000 cash received. No debt, expenses, losses or other property. Receiving some cash does not necessarily make all realized gain currently taxable. The basis preserves the deferred amount. Realized gain $140,000 $390,000 land + $30,000 cash - $280,000 old basis. Recognized gain $30,000 Lesser of the $140,000 realized gain and $30,000 cash boot under these assumptions. Deferred gain $110,000 $140,000 realized less $30,000 recognized; it has not disappeared. Replacement basis $280,000 $280,000 old basis - $30,000 cash + $30,000 recognized gain. Check: $390,000 value - $110,000 deferred gain. Reconcile boot, deferred gain and carryover basis in an otherwise qualifying exchange.

697.title: Apply the residence category before the FIRPTA rate
697.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
697.text: Apply the residence category before the FIRPTA rate Fictional cases. Qualifying residence use requires definite plans for buyer or family occupancy for at least 50% of used days in each of the first two 12-month periods; vacant days are excluded. A foreign individual sells a U.S. real-property interest. Assume no other exemption or withholding certificate. Is the buyer's residence use qualifying? Qualifying use; $290,000 Amount realized is at or below $300,000. The buyer-residence exception can eliminate withholding. Qualifying use; $900,000 Amount realized exceeds $300,000 but is not over $1 million. 10% of $900,000 = $90,000 withheld. Investment use; $290,000 The buyer-residence requirement is not satisfied. Price alone does not create the exception: general 15% = $43,500. Distinguish the qualifying buyer-residence exception, reduced rate and general rate.

698.title: Allocate withholding by the sellers' interests
698.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
698.text: Allocate withholding by the sellers' interests Fictional fully subject transaction with no exemption or alternative election. FTB Publication 1016 specifies 0.0333 for this computation. Total: $14,985; do not substitute an exact one-thirtieth and silently change the result. Seller A / 40% $450,000 sale x 40% x 0.0333 = $5,994. 5994 Seller B / 60% $450,000 sale x 60% x 0.0333 = $8,991. 8991 Apply the FTB decimal multiplier and ownership shares without confusing withholding with final tax.

699.title: The closing day determines who receives each day's rent
699.lessonTitle: Transfer taxes, gain, withholding, and prorations
699.text: The closing day determines who receives each day's rent Original contractual calculation, not a universal California closing-day convention. Expense reimbursement may run in the opposite direction. Fictional $3,100 August rent, all collected by the seller. Agreement uses actual days, closes August 12 and gives the closing day to the buyer. 11 + 20 = 31 days. Giving the closing day to the seller instead would shift one $100 day; a different contract changes the allocation. Seller period / 11 days August 1-11 $3,100 / 31 = $100 per day. Seller is entitled to $1,100. Buyer period / 20 days August 12-31 Count both August 12 and August 31: buyer is entitled to $2,000. Debit seller; credit buyer $2,000 At closing Seller already collected the buyer's share. The credit transfers that benefit through settlement. Count actual days inclusively from the contract-assigned closing day and apply the correct debit direction.

700.title: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
700.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
700.text: Recognize transfers that depend on death, court authority, or operation of law.

701.title: Authority replaces the ordinary owner signature
701.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
701.text: Determine the event, authorized signer, and required approvals before accepting a special-purpose deed; a title alone does not establish valid sale authority. In an ordinary sale, the living owner or an authorized representative executes the transaction. Special transfers require a different source of authority: death and succession law, a trust, a court order, a foreclosure power, or another statute. The salesperson's first task is to identify who has authority to act and what conditions limit that authority. A relative who has keys is not necessarily entitled to list a decedent's house. A beneficiary who expects to inherit is not necessarily the current title holder or authorized estate representative. A lender that holds a deed of trust has security rights, but not unlimited permission to sell outside the applicable foreclosure process. Distinguish ownership claims from power to administer. The person entitled to receive value from an estate may not be the person authorized to sign the deed during administration. Title and escrow providers commonly require evidence of capacity, appointment, powers, and any relevant orders.

702.title: Death does not produce one universal process
702.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
702.text: A will names beneficiaries and may nominate an executor, but appointment and the property's existing ownership determine who can act. A person who dies with a valid will is testate; a person whose property is not disposed of by a valid will may be intestate as to that property. A will directs disposition but does not itself guarantee that probate can be avoided. A person can also die partly testate and partly intestate if the will does not dispose of all probate property. Probate administration addresses assets, debts, claims, taxes, and distribution under court authority. An executor is nominated in the will and serves after the required appointment. An administrator is appointed when an executor does not serve, commonly where there is no will. Both are personal representatives and owe duties to the estate and interested persons. Intestate succession determines heirs under statute. It is not a rule that the closest person who volunteered to maintain the house owns it. Marital property characterization and family relationships can affect shares. If no entitled private successor exists under the governing law, escheat may result in property passing to the state.

703.title: A will, an appointment, and a deed do different work
703.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
703.text: Suppose a will leaves a house to a niece and nominates a nephew as executor. The niece is the intended beneficiary of that disposition; the nephew is the proposed administrator of the estate in the executor role. Neither fact alone shows that either person may immediately sign a listing or deed without the required authority. Court appointment and the scope of powers must be established where probate administration is necessary. The estate may need to pay debts or expenses before distributing property. A specific gift in a will does not guarantee the beneficiary will receive the asset unaffected by valid claims and administration requirements. Conversely, the personal representative's control during administration does not make the house the representative's personal property. For a transaction file, useful evidence can include the death certificate, relevant title documents, court letters, orders, and other authority documents appropriate to the proceeding. The exact requirements belong to the governing law and title review. A salesperson should identify the correct capacity and obtain verification, not choose a signer based on family seniority, possession of keys, or who first called the office.

704.title: Nonprobate transfers
704.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
704.text: Verify each nonprobate mechanism; a statutory transfer-on-death deed has execution and 60-day recording requirements, while summary succession uses procedure-specific limits. Some property passes outside ordinary probate. Valid joint-tenancy survivorship can transfer the deceased joint tenant's interest to surviving joint tenants. Community property with right of survivorship can provide a similar specified transfer mechanism. Appropriate documents are still needed to establish the death and update the record; survivorship does not mean the public title record updates itself. A properly funded trust allows the trustee to administer property under the trust's terms. A successor trustee's sale is not automatically the same as a court-confirmed probate sale. Review trust authority and any limits. A person named as a beneficiary is not necessarily empowered to sign for the trust. A valid transfer-on-death deed can transfer qualifying property under its statutory requirements. It is not equivalent to simply writing a beneficiary's name on an ordinary deed and leaving it unrecorded in a drawer. Under sections 5624 and 5626: The transferor signs and dates the deed. Two witnesses present at the same time witness the signing or the transferor's acknowledgment of the signature.A notary takes the acknowledgment. Record the deed no later than 60 days after that acknowledgment.Delivery to and acceptance by the beneficiary during the transferor's lifetime are not required. Property eligibility, revocation, and other statutory conditions still matter. California also provides simplified procedures for qualifying estates and property. For deaths on or after April 1, 2025, the primary-residence petition procedure under Probate Code sections 13151-13154 uses a $750,000 limit, subject to its other conditions. This is a simplified court process, not an exemption for every estate asset. Other procedures have different limits, and periodic adjustments are scheduled. Eligibility depends on property type, value, date of death, and the particular procedure; an old single "small estate limit" does not control every transfer.

705.title: Compare death, sale, and termination of a life estate
705.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
705.text: A life tenant's death ends that life estate according to its terms. The succeeding interest may belong to a remainderman or revert to the grantor or successors, depending on how it was created. The life tenant's will does not ordinarily convey a life estate beyond the measuring life. This differs from a fee owner's death, which leaves an inheritable ownership interest to be administered or transferred. Trust property presents another distinction. The successor trustee may have authority to sell under the trust even though no personal representative has been appointed for that property. But the trust must actually hold the relevant interest; merely signing a trust document without transferring the house into it does not establish that the house is administered as trust property. Survivorship requires verification as well. A deed originally creating joint tenancy may have been affected by a later conveyance or severance. The correct answer follows the interest existing at death, not an assumption based on how the owners first purchased. These examples explain why a death certificate answers who died but does not, by itself, identify every successor or signing authority.

706.title: Selling through probate
706.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
706.text: Check the representative's powers and applicable notice or confirmation process; independent administration does not remove fiduciary obligations or every procedural condition. A personal representative may sell estate property under the authority granted by the court and applicable law. Some sales require court confirmation; others may proceed under the Independent Administration of Estates Act with full authority and required notices, subject to objections and restrictions. Limited authority does not confer every power available under full authority. In a confirmation sale, the accepted offer can be subject to a hearing and qualifying overbids. The initial buyer should understand that acceptance by the representative is not necessarily the final transfer. The process protects the estate's interests, and the court evaluates statutory requirements rather than merely honoring whichever buyer arrived first. For an ordinary private real property sale requiring confirmation under Probate Code section 10309, both the appraisal and its valuation date must be within one year before the confirmation hearing, and the offered sum must be at least 90% of that appraised value. Statutory exceptions exist. Probate commissions are governed by the applicable contract and court authority; a salesperson should not assume the same payment procedure as an unrestricted private sale. Under Probate Code section 10311, the statutory minimum first overbid generally adds 10% of the first $10,000 of the accepted bid and 5% of the amount above $10,000. The hearing can involve further bidding and procedural requirements. This formula does not determine every later increment or apply to every trust or independently administered sale.

707.title: Independent administration is still administration
707.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
707.text: The Independent Administration of Estates Act can permit a personal representative with the required authority to act without obtaining a separate confirmation order for every qualifying sale. That does not eliminate fiduciary duties, notice requirements, restrictions in the appointment, or the effect of a proper objection. Full authority and limited authority must not be treated as identical. A buyer considering an estate sale should determine whether court confirmation is required and whether the offer is subject to additional procedural conditions. A transaction advertised as "probate" might proceed differently from another probate transaction because the representative's authority differs. The label alone does not establish an overbid hearing or guarantee that no hearing will occur. The representative must also distinguish estate expenses from personal expenses and handle proceeds for the estate. A brokerage should not disburse sale funds to a beneficiary merely because everyone expects that person eventually to inherit. Distribution authority, creditor claims, taxes, and the governing order or administration process may require a different destination and timing.

708.title: Worked overbid
708.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
708.text: Calculate the ordinary first-overbid minimum from the accepted bid, then separately examine appraisal requirements, bidder responsibility, terms, and judicial discretion. Suppose an accepted bid of $500,000 is presented for court confirmation and the statutory first-overbid formula applies. Ten percent of the first $10,000 is $1,000. Five percent of the remaining $490,000 is $24,500. Add both increments to $500,000 to obtain $525,500. Do not add 10% to the entire $500,000. Do not subtract the first $10,000 from the final bid. The first segment and the remaining segment use different rates, and both increments are added to the accepted bid. Deposit, qualification, and hearing rules must also be met; the arithmetic alone does not qualify someone to bid.

709.title: Appraisal threshold and overbid are separate calculations
709.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
709.text: Assume a private estate sale requires confirmation, the qualifying appraisal is $600,000, and no exception to the ordinary 90% rule applies. The threshold is $540,000. An accepted $550,000 offer clears that threshold. The first-overbid formula then uses the accepted $550,000 offer as its base, not the $600,000 appraisal. Ten percent of the first $10,000 is $1,000. Five percent of the remaining $540,000 is $27,000. Add $28,000 to the accepted offer to obtain $578,000. The $540,000 figure has two different appearances here: it is the minimum appraisal-based price and coincidentally the portion of the accepted bid above $10,000. Those are different calculations, and different numbers would eliminate the coincidence. If the accepted bid were only $520,000, computing an overbid would not by itself cure the original confirmation problem under the stated assumptions. First determine whether the sale satisfies applicable requirements. Then calculate the bidding threshold if the procedure calls for one. Price, bidder responsibility, payment terms, and judicial discretion remain separate considerations. Meeting the numerical first-overbid minimum is not an unconditional entitlement to confirmation. Probate Code section 10311 also addresses a responsible bidder, legal compliance, the court's discretion to order a new sale, and differing cash or credit terms. The formula uses the bid without deducting a broker's commission. A mathematically sufficient offer can still fail a different requirement.

710.title: Other involuntary and court-related transfers
710.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
710.text: Foreclosure, deed in lieu, partition, condemnation, and bankruptcy transfer interests through different processes; none universally removes every prior property right. Foreclosure enforces a security interest through the applicable judicial or nonjudicial process. A trustee's sale under a deed of trust and a judicial foreclosure are different procedures. Lien priority determines which interests may be extinguished and which may survive; buying at foreclosure does not guarantee a property free of every lien. A deed in lieu of foreclosure is a voluntary conveyance to the lender as an alternative to completing foreclosure. Because it is not the foreclosure process itself, junior interests are not automatically eliminated. The lender examines title and the parties' settlement carefully. A tax sale follows statutory enforcement of tax-defaulted property. A sheriff's sale can arise from execution of a judgment. A partition proceeding resolves cotenant interests through division or, when appropriate, sale and allocation of proceeds. Condemnation is the legal proceeding through which government exercises eminent domain, ordinarily requiring just compensation under the governing standards. Bankruptcy can place property under federal court control and impose an automatic stay. A creditor or broker should not assume that ordinary enforcement or closing can continue unchanged after learning of a filing. Court authority, trustee powers, liens, and exemptions may determine the next steps.

711.title: Match the event to the authority
711.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
711.text:
| Facts in the file | Governing question | Boundary to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cotenants cannot agree how to end their shared ownership. | Is division or a court-ordered sale appropriate under partition law? | A partition resolves ownership interests; it is not a foreclosure for unpaid debt. |
| An agency seeks land for a public road. | Does the taking satisfy eminent-domain authority, public use, and just-compensation requirements? | A public purpose does not turn a taking into a gift or ordinary probate transfer. |
| A parcel has become tax defaulted. | Has the tax collector's statutory power of sale arisen and have the required procedures been followed? | The first missed installment does not itself authorize an immediate tax auction. Property category and statutory exceptions can affect timing. |
| A debtor files bankruptcy before a scheduled enforcement step. | Does the automatic stay apply, and has any required relief from it been obtained? | An existing sale date is not permission to ignore a stay; statutory exceptions and court orders must be checked. | Change the tax-sale facts. With no special exception or other bar, an ordinary residential parcel only two years into tax default has not reached section 3691's five-year power-of-sale period. Specified nonresidential commercial property generally has a three-year period, but a county can elect five years. These periods begin at tax default, not merely at the first missed installment, and do not replace the required sale procedures.

712.title: A special deed does not answer every title question
712.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
712.text: An investor buys at a foreclosure sale and later learns that a senior deed of trust remains. The phrase "foreclosure property" did not promise a debt-free asset. Determine the lien foreclosed, its priority, the procedure, and which interests survived. A deed in lieu raises a different issue because a voluntary conveyance does not perform the same extinguishment process. Partition and condemnation also differ in purpose. Partition resolves competing ownership interests among cotenants through division or sale as appropriate. Condemnation implements a public acquisition under eminent-domain authority. Both can involve a court and a resulting conveyance, but neither should be classified as ordinary probate merely because a judge participates. The exam method is to identify the event, the authority, and the resulting interest. Death, default, unpaid taxes, cotenant disagreement, and public acquisition trigger different rules. The name of the resulting deed helps identify the process, but the proceeding and valid authority determine what the buyer receives.

713.title: Transfers through operation of law
713.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
713.text: Adverse possession requires qualifying possession and timely assessed-tax payments; gradual natural accretion and public dedication follow different rules and exceptions. Adverse possession can produce ownership after strict requirements are satisfied. Code of Civil Procedure section 325(b) requires five years of continuous occupation and claim and timely payment of all state, county, and municipal taxes levied and assessed on the land during that period. Qualifying possession must also be established; paying another owner's taxes alone does not transfer title. A prescriptive easement concerns a use right rather than ownership. Civil Code section 1007 prevents ordinary adverse possession from ripening against the public property and dedicated public uses it protects. Accession can alter ownership boundaries through events such as gradual accretion. Under Civil Code section 1014, land forming imperceptibly along a river or stream from natural accumulation or recession belongs to the bank owner, subject to an existing right of way. Do not substitute a sudden channel change or artificial fill for those stated facts. Dedication can create public rights through the owner's acts and required acceptance. Mere public use is not a universal shortcut: Civil Code section 1009 limits when public use can mature into permanent rights and specifies qualifications, including certain publicly funded improvements and coastal property. A path used by visitors therefore requires investigation of the actual dedication and use history, not an assumption that it became public automatically.

714.title: Exam review
714.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
714.text: Trace authority, procedure, and the interest transferred independently; a high price or familiar deed label does not cure missing approval. Identify the authority, proceeding, and interest transferred. A will does not itself avoid probate; a trust sale does not automatically require court confirmation; an expected heir cannot automatically sign for an estate. Apply the probate overbid formula only when the question makes it relevant, and never assume a special-purpose deed erases all prior rights.

715.title: Probate, court sales, and other transfers: core distinctions
715.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
715.text: Authority Identify the representative's actual authority, not just family or beneficiary status. Procedure Probate confirmation, independent administration, and nonprobate transfers differ. Bidding The appraisal floor and first-overbid increment use different bases.

716.title: The appraisal floor is not the overbid
716.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
716.text: An ordinary probate private sale requires court confirmation. The appraisal and valuation dates satisfy the applicable one-year requirements, and the appraised value is $840,000. The accepted bid is $780,000. Apply the ordinary ninety-percent appraisal threshold and the statutory first-overbid calculation. Assume no exception changes these numerical rules; all other confirmation requirements remain separate. Use the appraisal only for the appraisal requirement and the accepted bid only for the overbid increment. Then return to authority and procedure. The arithmetic is a threshold analysis, not a substitute for examining whether the court may confirm this particular offer.

717.title: Ninety percent of appraisal is the overbid.
717.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
717.text: Calculate the two requirements independently. They use different bases and serve different purposes.

718.title: Subtract commission before calculating the increment.
718.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
718.text: Use the accepted bid as the statute directs. Compensation does not redefine the statutory bid amount.

719.title: The highest numerical offer must always win.
719.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
719.text: Check responsibility, terms, legal compliance, and discretion. A sufficient number does not satisfy every confirmation condition.

720.title: The appraisal floor is not the overbid: Check the appraisal floor
720.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
720.text: Appraised value $840,000 Accepted bid $780,000 Appraisal threshold 90% of appraised value First-overbid increment 10% of first $10,000; 5% of remainder 840000 * 0.90 756000 The accepted $780,000 bid exceeds the $756,000 floor. This comparison addresses the ordinary private-sale appraisal requirement, not the amount a competing bidder must offer. A bid below this floor is not cured merely by correctly calculating an increment from an inadequate accepted price.

721.title: The appraisal floor is not the overbid: Calculate the first bracket
721.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
721.text: Appraised value $840,000 Accepted bid $780,000 Appraisal threshold 90% of appraised value First-overbid increment 10% of first $10,000; 5% of remainder 10000 * 0.10 1000 The first $10,000 of the accepted bid receives a ten-percent increment, producing $1,000. Do not apply ten percent to the full $780,000 or to the appraisal. The statute uses a two-part increment because the first bracket and the remaining bid have different rates.

722.title: The appraisal floor is not the overbid: Calculate the remaining bracket
722.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
722.text: Appraised value $840,000 Accepted bid $780,000 Appraisal threshold 90% of appraised value First-overbid increment 10% of first $10,000; 5% of remainder 770000 * 0.05 38500 Subtract the first $10,000 from the accepted bid, leaving $770,000. Five percent of that remainder is $38,500. The commission is not deducted to create a net accepted bid for this formula. A broker's compensation question is separate from the statutory calculation base.

723.title: The appraisal floor is not the overbid: Add the increment to the bid
723.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
723.text: Appraised value $840,000 Accepted bid $780,000 Appraisal threshold 90% of appraised value First-overbid increment 10% of first $10,000; 5% of remainder 780000 + 1000 + 38500 819500 The calculated minimum first overbid is $819,500. Reaching that amount does not establish an unconditional right to purchase. Responsible-bidder requirements, legal compliance, cash or credit terms, and the court's statutory discretion can still affect confirmation or result in a new sale.

724.title: The appraisal floor is not the overbid: Verify with an equivalent expression
724.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
724.text: Appraised value $840,000 Accepted bid $780,000 Appraisal threshold 90% of appraised value First-overbid increment 10% of first $10,000; 5% of remainder 780000 * 1.05 + 500 819500 For an original bid of at least $10,000, five percent of the entire bid plus an extra $500 produces the same increment as the two statutory brackets. The extra $500 supplies the additional five percent on the first $10,000. This arithmetic cross-check does not remove appraisal, bidder, terms, or court-approval requirements.

725.title: After a death, identify title and authority first
725.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
725.text: After a death, identify title and authority first This is a classification map, not a finding that a particular estate qualifies for a procedure. Heirship, a will, and legal authority to sign a sale instrument are different questions. How was this interest held? Survivorship interest Determine whether a valid survivorship form controls. Verify the documents needed to establish the survivor's title. Trust-held interest Determine the successor trustee and powers granted. Verify trustee authority and transaction requirements. Estate interest Determine whether probate or another authorized procedure applies. Verify representative authority and any court requirements.

726.title: Build the first overbid from the accepted offer
726.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
726.text: Build the first overbid from the accepted offer Assume this court-confirmed sale uses the stated statutory formula. The accepted offer, not the appraisal, supplies this base; bidder eligibility and court requirements remain separate. Accepted offer subject to the stated first-overbid rule 550000 10% of the first $10,000 1000 5% of the remaining $540,000 27000 Calculated first-overbid minimum 578000 $550,000 accepted offer + $28,000 combined increments.

727.title: An appointment order is not yet effective authority
727.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
727.text: An appointment order is not yet effective authority Original authority timeline. Limited preappointment preservation acts do not create general authority to sell the house. Fictional estate requiring probate. A named executor wants to sell estate real property; no other independent capacity is established. A signed order alone is not enough. Section 8400 separately permits a nominated executor to pay funeral expenses and take necessary preservation measures before appointment. Nominated executor Will reviewed Being named is not an effective appointment to administer the estate. Appointment ordered Order entered The court makes the appointment, but the order does not become effective until letters issue. Appointment effective Letters issued Now examine the powers, notice requirements and any sale restrictions before proceeding. Identify issuance of letters as the point at which a personal representative appointment becomes effective.

728.title: A trustee's power reaches trust property
728.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
728.text: A trustee's power reaches trust property Fictional asset map. Different ownership evidence or a court determination can change the result; a trust document alone does not establish title to every asset. Successor trustee Assume valid succession. Read the trust terms and any limits on statutory sale powers. Funded residence Trust property Verified records establish the house as trust property. Evaluate the trustee's sale authority. Separate vacant lot Title unproven The lot remains outside the stipulated trust assets. The trustee title alone does not authorize its sale. Beneficiary Beneficial interest An expected distribution does not by itself make the beneficiary the authorized grantor of trust property. Separate trustee authority from a claim to administer an asset the trust does not own.

729.title: Read the letters before choosing a probate sale route
729.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
729.text: Read the letters before choosing a probate sale route Fictional routing test. Full authority does not remove notices, fiduciary duties, valid objections or appointment restrictions. What authority has actually been granted for this estate real-property sale? Full independent authority The representative has the qualifying power and complies with the proposed-action procedure and restrictions. A sale can proceed without ordinary court confirmation where the applicable requirements are satisfied. Limited independent authority The representative lacks full authority for the real-property sale. Do not import the full-authority exception to ordinary sale supervision. Only a family statement A relative says the estate is independent, but no authority documents have been examined. The label is insufficient. Verify appointment and powers before promising either route. Distinguish full independent authority, limited authority and unresolved authority.

730.title: A recent report can use an appraisal date that is too old
730.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
730.text: A recent report can use an appraisal date that is too old Original appraisal review specimen, not a court form. A qualifying new appraisal may be needed under the governing procedure. Private probate sale / Confirmation check Fictional October 20, 2026 confirmation hearing. Assume the ordinary section 10309 rule and no statutory exception. Check authority, both dates, then price. Passing the percentage test does not satisfy every confirmation requirement. Appraisal completed September 1, 2026 This date is within one year of the hearing. Valuation date used August 1, 2025 This separate date is more than one year before the hearing and fails the ordinary requirement. Appraised value $900,000 90% would be $810,000, but a price calculation does not cure the stale valuation date. Accepted offer $830,000 It exceeds $810,000, yet the appraisal-date problem remains. Check both appraisal completion and valuation dates before applying the 90-percent private-sale test.

731.title: Compute the first overbid before deducting commission
731.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
731.text: Compute the first overbid before deducting commission Fictional section 10311 example. A responsible bidder, legally compliant offer, applicable terms and the court's powers remain relevant. Original bid, before any commission 760000 10% of first $10,000 1000 5% of remaining $750,000 37500 Minimum first overbid 798500 $760,000 + $1,000 + $37,500. Do not subtract the broker's compensation from the base. Use the original bid, not net proceeds after brokerage compensation, for the statutory first overbid.

732.title: A voluntary deed does not perform a lien-priority sale
732.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
732.text: A voluntary deed does not perform a lien-priority sale Fictional title relationships. The cited servicing requirements are program-specific; the illustration does not promise that any lender will accept a deed in lieu. Deed to first lender Proposed deed in lieu, not a completed trustee's foreclosure sale. First lender Proposed grantee Reviews the settlement and title; accepting a deed is not the same extinguishment process as foreclosure. Junior lienholder Separate lien The owner's voluntary deed does not automatically release this claim. Title clearance Release required Fannie Mae's cited program requires resolving title issues, including subordinate releases, so clear and marketable title can be conveyed. Identify why a subordinate lien must still be addressed in a deed-in-lieu transaction.

733.title: Five years alone is not an adverse-possession checklist
733.lessonTitle: Probate, court sales, and other transfers
733.text: Five years alone is not an adverse-possession checklist Fictional issue spotting. Section 325 also addresses possession and occupation; neither paying a bill nor using land alone proves title. A person asserts ownership after occupying land for five years. Which additional fact changes the claim? Assessed taxes unpaid The claimant and qualifying predecessors did not timely pay the taxes levied and assessed for the required period. The required tax condition is missing; occupancy duration does not cure it. Publicly owned parcel The occupied property belongs to the state or another public entity. Section 1007 prevents possession from ripening into a right against that owner. Taxes paid on private land Certified tax records support timely payments, but the other possession requirements remain disputed. Tax payment is necessary on these facts, not sufficient proof of every element. Identify decisive failures involving assessed taxes or protected public property.

734.title: Licensing, supervision, and consumer protection
734.text: Who may perform licensed work, how brokers supervise it, and how California enforces professional standards.

735.title: The activity determines the license
735.text: Identify the act, expected compensation, person represented, and actual exemption before deciding whether the worker needs an active license and broker affiliation. A real estate license gives permission to perform defined activities; it is not a general credential for every business connected with land. California ordinarily requires a broker license when a person, for compensation or in expectation of compensation, acts for another to sell, buy, lease, negotiate, solicit, or perform other statutorily defined real estate services. Arranging certain secured loans and selling business opportunities also fall within the law. One transaction can be enough. Calling a fee a consulting payment does not change the underlying activity. An owner dealing with the owner's own property generally is not acting for another. Other exemptions exist for specified persons and functions, including certain court-appointed fiduciaries. Exemptions have boundaries: being an attorney, accountant, relative, or experienced investor does not create unrestricted authority to conduct a brokerage business. On the exam, identify who owns the property, whose interests the worker serves, what the worker actually does, and whether compensation is expected. A salesperson performs licensed activity through an employing or responsible broker. Passing the examination alone is insufficient. The license must be issued and effective, and the necessary broker affiliation must exist before the salesperson begins licensed work. A salesperson cannot independently establish a brokerage merely by creating a company or calling the business a real estate team.

736.title: Supervision is an operating responsibility
736.text: Reasonable supervision requires implemented procedures, document review, and responses to warning signs; a contractor agreement or delegated task does not erase responsibility. The responsible broker must maintain reasonable supervision over transactions and personnel. This includes reviewing documents, establishing trust fund procedures, monitoring advertising, maintaining records, preventing discrimination, and making sure personnel understand their authority. An office manual that nobody implements is not effective supervision. Nor does an independent-contractor agreement eliminate the broker's duties under licensing law. A broker can assign operational tasks to qualified people, including a branch manager where applicable. Delegation does not automatically eliminate the responsible broker's accountability. A salesperson should elevate unusual contract language, trust shortages, disputed releases, suspected fraud, and demands to conceal defects. These are matters for timely professional judgment, not problems to hide until closing. The salesperson normally receives compensation for licensed work through the responsible broker. A seller cannot bypass that relationship by paying the salesperson a separate negotiating fee directly. Referral compensation also requires attention to licensing and the service performed. A broker cannot pay an unlicensed person for performing acts that required a license simply because the payment occurs after closing.

737.title: Assistants can support, but cannot replace, licensees
737.text: An assistant may transmit approved information or schedule events, but independent negotiation, substantive advice, and selection of transaction terms cross the clerical boundary. The distinction between administrative work and licensed work is functional. An assistant may organize files, schedule inspections, obtain status information, deliver approved materials, and perform permitted document preparation under supervision. An assistant may check whether signatures are present; the licensee makes the final determination about compliance and advises the client about consequences. An assistant cannot independently explain which counteroffer to accept, negotiate price, solicit a particular listing through substantive persuasion, or interpret an agreement for a buyer. At an open house, handing out prepared brochures and arranging contact with the licensee differ from conducting a property showing or answering negotiating questions. A broker's presence does not transform prohibited conduct into authorized conduct. Consider a caller asking when an inspection report will arrive. The assistant can obtain its delivery status. If the caller asks whether the report justifies canceling the purchase, the assistant should transfer the question to a licensee. This boundary remains the same whether communication occurs by telephone, text, social media, or a website chatbot. Technology does not acquire a license by automating the conversation.

738.title: Initial qualification and renewal
738.text: Passing an examination, meeting renewal education requirements, and holding present authority to practice are separate milestones; a late-renewal opportunity does not authorize intervening work. Salesperson applicants ordinarily must be at least 18 and complete the required prelicense education, including Real Estate Principles, Real Estate Practice, and an approved additional course, before satisfying examination and licensing requirements. Required practice-course content includes fair housing and implicit bias. Honesty and disclosure in the application process matter independently of a passing score; fingerprints and background review are part of licensing. California real estate licenses generally run for four years. Renewal ordinarily requires 45 hours of DRE-approved continuing education completed within the applicable period. For a salesperson's first renewal, current requirements include specified courses in ethics, agency, trust funds, risk management, fair housing with an interactive component, and implicit bias, plus minimum consumer-protection coursework. Broker requirements and later renewals have different mandatory-course arrangements. A salesperson should not apply the broker's first-renewal list without checking the correct category. Late renewal may be available within two years after expiration, but that opportunity does not authorize licensed activity during the lapse. A qualifying on-time renewal is different: Business and Professions Code section 10156.2 permits continued operation under the existing license after its stated expiration when the prescribed application, renewal fee and good-faith evidence of continuing-education compliance are timely filed, and the license was not previously suspended or revoked. DRE can subsequently notify the applicant of limits on continuation. A late application cannot borrow that protection. Separate present authority, timely renewal and late-renewal eligibility.

739.title: Records make conduct reviewable
739.text: Retain the transaction's evidence, not merely its final contract; electronic messages and instructions can explain representations, receipt, authority, and delivery. Business and Professions Code section 10148 generally requires brokers to retain transaction records for three years from closing or, if a transaction is not consummated, from the listing date. The statutory categories include listings, receipts, canceled checks, trust records, and other documents obtained or executed in connection with transactions requiring a license. Special laws or circumstances may justify or require longer retention. Electronic records must remain accessible, accurate, and reproducible for examination. Keeping only the final contract can omit important offers, instructions, disclosures, and evidence of delivery. Deleting a message because the application labels it a chat does not eliminate its significance to a transaction. A defensible file tells the story of what was represented, authorized, received, and delivered.

740.title: Discipline and financial recovery serve different purposes
740.text: Administrative discipline addresses licensing conduct, while civil remedies and the limited Recovery Account have different purposes, eligibility rules, procedures, and financial limits. DRE licenses and regulates real estate professionals and can investigate, impose appropriate administrative sanctions, suspend or revoke licenses, and issue orders concerning unlicensed activity. Grounds can include fraud, substantial misrepresentation, trust fund violations, and failure of supervision. An ordinary commission disagreement does not automatically establish a disciplinary violation, and a DRE complaint is not a substitute for a civil damages action. The Consumer Recovery Account, historically called the recovery fund, provides limited compensation for eligible actual, direct losses involving licensee fraud or trust fund conversion in transactions requiring a license. The claimant must satisfy statutory procedures, ordinarily including a qualifying final judgment, award, or order and collection requirements. The current maximum is $50,000 per transaction and an aggregate $250,000 per licensee. Multiple victims do not each receive an unlimited separate transaction cap.An application generally must be filed within one year after the qualifying determination becomes final.Payment can trigger license suspension until statutory repayment requirements are met.

741.title: Worked scenario
741.text: A license lapse and an assistant's unauthorized showing create separate authorization problems; the broker must reassign work rather than rely on pending renewal. Morgan's license expired yesterday, and no on-time renewal was filed. A late application is being prepared, and the broker asks Morgan to negotiate a buyer's counteroffer while an unlicensed assistant handles the open house alone. Neither instruction solves the authorization problem. Morgan must stop licensed work during the lapse; the assistant must remain within permitted administrative duties. The broker should reassign negotiations and licensed showing work to properly authorized personnel, document the arrangements, and correct the office's expiration tracking. If a later dispute arises, complete records let the broker distinguish a communication error from unauthorized activity. A client's loss would not automatically qualify for the Consumer Recovery Account: the claimant must show the specific statutory basis and satisfy the recovery process.

742.title: Apply the licensing test to a workflow
742.text: Changing from typing a licensee's chosen terms to independently choosing a contingency changes the activity, even when the same standard form is used. Consider three workers at the same property. The owner's employee schedules a repair, a brokerage assistant sends an approved inspection appointment, and a salesperson recommends a counteroffer. Although all work concerns real estate, the legal analysis is not identical. Identify the act, whether it is performed for another, whether compensation is expected, and whether a specific exemption applies. Then determine whether the individual is properly authorized within the required broker relationship. Do not start with a job title and work backward toward an exemption. An assistant may type information supplied by the licensee into an approved form without independently selecting the terms. If the assistant chooses the contingency period based on the buyer's needs, the task has changed from clerical preparation to substantive judgment. Likewise, transmitting an already authorized message differs from bargaining over whether the seller should pay for repairs. A script or supervisor's eventual review does not necessarily make an otherwise licensed act clerical. Suppose a team leader tells an assistant to call potential sellers and persuade them that now is the right time to list. Calling the worker a marketing coordinator does not change the solicitation. A safer workflow separates permitted contact or scheduling functions from the licensed conversation and provides an immediate transfer to an authorized person. The relevant DRE guidance is function-specific; an office should train workers on boundaries, not simply hand them a list of approved job titles.

743.title: Build supervision around evidence
743.text: Design supervision around actual risks and evidence; repeated late deposit documentation calls for investigation before a financial loss is established. A responsible broker cannot personally attend every conversation, but can implement controls that make problems visible. Before assigning a transaction, verify authorization and relevant experience. During the transaction, review material documents, changes, advertising, deadlines, and money handling. After closing or cancellation, check that the retained file includes the instructions and disclosures needed to explain what occurred. These controls should match the brokerage's activities: a firm holding rent reserves has different operational exposure from one sending every purchase deposit directly to neutral escrow. For example, a salesperson repeatedly turns in deposit receipts several days late. The absence of a known loss does not make the pattern harmless. The broker should investigate when the funds actually arrived, where they went, whether required deadlines were met, and whether the office's instructions were followed. Coaching alone may be insufficient if access or assignment changes are needed. A signed acknowledgment of the office manual is evidence of training, not proof that later transactions complied. The same reasoning applies to a remote branch. Digital access to files can support supervision, but only if someone reviews the relevant information and follows up. A manager's appointment is not permission for the responsible broker to ignore warning signs. The appropriate exam answer usually addresses the conduct and the oversight process rather than treating delegation as a complete transfer of responsibility.

744.title: Separate the remedy from the complaint
744.text: Match the requested result to the available process, and never confuse correcting records or renewing a license with retroactively authorizing earlier conduct. Imagine a buyer alleges that an agent deliberately concealed a serious defect and seeks repayment of repair costs. Several processes may arise from the same facts. DRE examines licensing violations. A court or other authorized forum determines civil claims and available relief. An association may evaluate its member's code obligations. Each has different authority, procedures, and potential outcomes; filing in one place does not automatically accomplish the purpose of another. The Consumer Recovery Account is narrower than general errors-and-omissions coverage. An unsuccessful investment, a normal commission disagreement, or simple dissatisfaction with service does not by itself satisfy its eligibility rules. Even an eligible fraud loss must pass through the required determination and collection process. If several people claim losses from the same transaction, the transaction limit matters collectively, and the licensee aggregate remains a separate ceiling. The existence of two ceilings does not allow a claimant to choose whichever yields more. Finally, distinguish correcting a problem from erasing it. Renewing an expired license restores authority only as applicable prospectively; it does not make earlier unauthorized negotiations proper. Reconstructing missing records may help explain a file, but fabricated or backdated records create a new problem. An exam scenario that offers concealment as an efficient solution is testing honesty and accountability as much as the underlying licensing rule.

745.title: Exam review
745.text: Resolve licensing questions by function, authority, supervision, and remedy; avoid answers that treat job labels, client consent, or subsequent renewal as universal permission. Identify the licensed act before analyzing a worker's title or payment method.A salesperson acts through the responsible broker; supervision cannot be waived by contract.Clerical delivery and status reporting differ from negotiation and advice.A renewal opportunity is not permission to practice with an expired license.DRE discipline, civil remedies, and Consumer Recovery Account payments are separate processes.

746.title: Licensing, supervision, and consumer protection: core distinctions
746.text: Activity first Licensing follows what a person does for another, not the worker's title. Delegation is limited A manager can perform assigned work without eliminating the responsible broker's supervision. Remedies differ DRE discipline, civil damages, and Consumer Recovery Account eligibility require separate analyses.

747.title: A counteroffer arrives during a license lapse
747.text: A remote team receives a counteroffer after its lead salesperson's license expired without an on-time renewal. An unlicensed coordinator knows the file, the branch manager is available, and the client wants an immediate response. The manager asks the coordinator to choose a shorter inspection period and promises to review the signed paperwork later. The first control is a qualified person performing the right function at the right time. Review and accurate records support that authority; they cannot create it retroactively.

748.title: The manager signed, so supervision transferred.
748.text: Treat management as delegated performance, not an automatic release. The responsible broker must still maintain reasonable oversight.

749.title: No closing means no licensed activity.
749.text: Evaluate the negotiation when it occurred. One compensated act can matter before a sale is completed.

750.title: A complaint guarantees recovery.
750.text: Identify the specific remedy and statutory prerequisites. Discipline and compensation are not interchangeable processes.

751.title: A counteroffer arrives during a license lapse: Classify the proposed work
751.text: Separate transmission of the counteroffer from deciding whether its inspection term serves the client. Forwarding approved information can be administrative; selecting the response is substantive. Identify who chose the term, what instructions already existed, and whether the worker was authorized when the choice was made. A standard form does not make every decision entered into it clerical.

752.title: A counteroffer arrives during a license lapse: Verify present authority
752.text: Confirm the status and required affiliation of the person who will advise the client. Reassign licensed work to an appropriately authorized licensee rather than waiting for the expired salesperson's renewal. Keep the current status check and assignment record with the transaction's communications. A pending late application or later renewal does not establish authority during this lapse.

753.title: A counteroffer arrives during a license lapse: Implement supervision now
753.text: The branch manager should arrange timely qualified assistance, review the proposed response, and escalate the office's expiration-control failure to the responsible broker. Document the review, the corrected assignment, and the procedure used to prevent another lapse. Delegation and independent-contractor status do not remove the responsible broker's supervisory role.

754.title: A counteroffer arrives during a license lapse: Preserve the actual history
754.text: Retain the original counteroffer, communications, actual dates, and corrective steps. If unauthorized advice already occurred, address that conduct rather than rewriting the file to imply earlier approval. A complete record distinguishes the client's decision from the coordinator's actions and the broker's response. Absence of a completed loss does not make inaccurate records acceptable.

755.title: A supervision system follows the work
755.text: A supervision system follows the work Written policies are part of supervision, not a replacement for it. Assigning a task does not by itself eliminate the responsible broker's supervisory duty. Set the scope Assign tasks within each person's license and authority. Set the procedure Give clear requirements for documents, trust funds, and disclosures. Review performance Check actual work and respond to exceptions and warning signs. Correct and document Address deficiencies and preserve required records.

756.title: The caller's question can change who must respond
756.text: The caller's question can change who must respond A broker's presence does not license an assistant to negotiate or interpret agreements. Classify the actual task, not the employee's title or communication channel. Is the request administrative, or does it require licensed judgment? When will the report arrive? The caller needs delivery status, not advice about the transaction. An assistant may obtain and communicate permitted status information. Should I cancel over the report? The caller needs interpretation or advice about contractual consequences. Refer the question to the responsible licensee.

757.title: One changed role changes the licensing analysis
757.text: One changed role changes the licensing analysis Fictional roles. Test actual functions and any specific exemption; this is not a list of all exempt activities. Owner sells own building Acts for self, not another. The ordinary broker definition does not attach on that fact alone. Consultant negotiates owner's sale Acts for another and expects a fee. The consulting label does not remove the licensed activity. Salesperson negotiates for client Performs brokerage activity. Must work through the responsible broker. Identify acting for another and expected compensation rather than relying on a job label.

758.title: Two recovery limits apply at the same time
758.text: Two recovery limits apply at the same time Fictional limit calculation for one new transaction with $70,000 of otherwise eligible uncompensated direct loss. Assume the prior payments remain counted and no competing pending claims or other adjustment. Eligibility, approval, and statutory proration are separate issues; these lines are ceilings, not promised payments. Multiple victims of one transaction share its limit. Prior payments counted against this licensee Ceiling for the stated claim With $225,000 already counted against the licensee limit, only $25,000 of aggregate capacity remains. A $70,000 eligible loss cannot bypass that limit by invoking the $50,000 transaction cap. Lower of $50,000 or unused $250,000 aggregate 0 50000 200000 50000 225000 25000 240000 10000 250000 0 Compute the lower ceiling from the transaction limit and remaining aggregate capacity without treating either limit as a guaranteed award.

759.title: The expiration date is not the only renewal fact
759.text: The expiration date is not the only renewal fact Both fictional licensees reach the printed expiration date. The filing facts, not the calendar label alone, distinguish their authority. Timely qualifying filing Prescribed application, fee, and good-faith CE evidence filed on time. No prior suspension or revocation.
